paper_sections.title: BOLD signal changes: location and size of signal maxima

description.value: The study used the Semantic Object Retrieval Test during fMRI to characterize semantic memory retrieval and its neural correlates in Gulf War veterans classified with Syndromes 1, 2, or 3 and matched deployed controls.

spans.text: We sought to characterize the disruptions in semantic memory retrieval, and the neural correlates of those disruptions, by using the SORT while acquiring fMRI data in veterans classified with Syndromes 1, 2, or 3, as well as in matched controls who were deployed to the region during the conflict but did not return with symptomatic complaints.

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional comparison of four groups of male Persian Gulf War veterans during a week-long multimodal neuroimaging and biomarker study conducted in 2008 and 2009; participants were classified by Gulf War Illness syndrome or as deployed controls.

spans.text: Subjects were housed and monitored at The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center’s Clinical and Translational Research Center (CTRC) in 2008 and 2009 and underwent a week-long multi-modal neuroimaging and biomarker study.

Semantic Object Retrieval Test (SORT)

description.value: Participants viewed pairs of written words representing features of common objects and decided whether the pair elicited retrieval of a specific object or a nonretrieval.

spans.text: retrievals

description.value: Word pairs that elicited retrieval of a specific object.

spans.text: stimulus pairs that have been shown in previous work (Assaf et al. 2006) to elicit retrieval of a specific object
nonretrievals

description.value: Re-paired feature words that did not elicit retrieval of a specific object.

spans.text: The same feature words that were used in the object-retrieval pairs were re-paired to form the nonretrieval pairs.
The stimuli were presented as an event-related design

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed that the target had to be a specific object rather than merely an association between the two words and to respond as fast as possible by pressing one button for retrievals and another for nonretrievals.

spans.text: Instructions for the task require subjects to respond as fast as possible by pressing one button for retrievals and another button for nonretrievals.
